holidays.name: National Lemon Chiffon Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the light, airy, citrus-kissed cake that tastes like sunshine in dessert form. Bakers and dessert lovers whip up egg whites, zest lemons, and enjoy a slice with a cup of tea.
holidays.origin: Lemon chiffon cake was invented by insurance salesman turned caterer Harry Baker in Los Angeles in the 1920s. He kept the recipe secret for about 20 years before selling it to General Mills in 1947.
holidays.funFact: Harry Baker's chiffon cake was served at the famous Brown Derby restaurant in Hollywood, and he guarded the recipe so closely that even his customers had no idea how he got the cake so fluffy. The secret was using vegetable oil instead of butter.

holidays.name: National Mom and Pop Business Owners Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the small, family-run shops, diners, and stores that give neighborhoods their character. People are encouraged to skip the big chains and spend some money at the corner bakery or hardware store.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance was created to recognize independent family-owned businesses and the entrepreneurs who run them. It is celebrated each year on March 29 across the United States.
holidays.funFact: Small businesses make up over 99 percent of all businesses in the United States, so chances are good that your favorite local spot qualifies for the celebration.

holidays.name: Niagara Falls Runs Dry Remembrance Day
holidays.description: A day to remember the eerie moment in 1848 when the thundering Niagara Falls fell silent and people woke to find the roar had vanished. Locals walked out onto the exposed riverbed to pick up souvenirs and relics.
holidays.origin: On March 29, 1848, an ice jam in Lake Erie blocked the flow of water into the Niagara River, and the falls slowed to a trickle for about 30 hours. The mysterious silence terrified many residents, who thought it was a sign of the end of the world.
holidays.funFact: During the dry spell, people found old bayonets, muskets, and tomahawks on the exposed riverbed, and some brave folks even walked out to rocks normally hidden beneath the rushing water.

holidays.name: Brae Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the Scottish hillsides in a quirky, wee way, encouraging folks to take a stroll up a brae and enjoy the view. A great excuse to put on boots, bring a flask of something warm, and shout at the scenery.
holidays.origin: Brae is a Scots word for a steep bank or hillside, and the observance grew up in online lists of quirky days as a light-hearted nod to Scottish language and landscape.
holidays.funFact: The word brae shows up in many Scottish place names and in the famous song Ye Banks and Braes o' Bonnie Doon by Robert Burns.

holidays.name: Texas Rangers Day Celebration of Coffee Break Culture
holidays.description: A playful observance of the humble work break, honoring the people who keep productivity alive with a cup of joe and a snack. Take a moment to step away from your desk and sip something warm.
holidays.origin: Coffee breaks became a staple of American workplaces in the 1950s, when the Pan-American Coffee Bureau popularized the slogan Give yourself a coffee break and get what coffee gives to you.
holidays.funFact: The coffee break is often traced to Norwegian and Swedish immigrant communities in Wisconsin in the 1800s, where wives would bring coffee and pastries to workers midday.
